`RustTpslViewUtil.getTPSLTriggerOrLimitTypeSpKey` (RustTpslViewUtil.kt:31-34):

```kotlin
"${TradeUIExtraKeys.TP_LIMIT_TRIGGER_TYPE}-${TradeCoreProxy.isSimulateLine()}-$uuid"
```
where `TradeUIExtraKeys.TP_LIMIT_TRIGGER_TYPE == "tp_limit_trigger_type"`
(TradeUIExtraKeys.kt:180) and `isSimulateLine` renders via Kotlin

literal `"null"` (Kotlin string-interpolation of `String?`).

Kotlin caller reads zero `TradeCoreProxy` state. Both the sim-line bool and
the uuid come from the same `CoreUserManager` session the native path reads.

`TradeCoreProxy.getTrade()?.getLoginUuid()` (a `String?`), so when not logged
in the suffix is the literal `"null"`. [`CTTradeAccountManager::uuid`]
returns `""` when not logged in, so to keep byte-for-byte parity we emit the
literal `"null"` for the empty case.

`PositionAssetManager::build_position_config_flags` and echoed into
`OKTPositionAssetListState::config_flags`.

Native source mapping (so Kotlin drops the `TradeCoreProxy` reads):
- `is_equal_or_greater_single_account` → `getTradeDataSettings().isEqualOrGreaterSingleAccount()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:343-344`)
- `support_all_instruments` → `getTradeConfig().isSupportAllInstruments()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:345`)
- `support_one_click_repay` → `getTradeConfig().isSupportOneClickRepay()`
(`RustFilterPositionsFragment.kt:346`)
- `is_demo` → `getCurrentSystemStatus() == DEMO_TRADING.headerValue`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:1118`; same demo session predicate)
- `is_auto_transfer` → `getTradeDataSettings().isFutureOpenPositionTrans()`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:1061`, gates the adjust-margin auto-transfer
path). Mirrors the existing manager derive at
`position_asset_manager.rs:718` (`get_future_iso_transfer_mode() ==
TRADE_ISO_MODE_OPEN_POSITION`).
- `is_pro` → `OKAppService.isPro()` / `TradeConfig.isPro()`
(`RustPositionListFragment.kt:386,603`, gates the last-price dialog
"Learn more" button). There is NO Rust producer for pro-app-mode yet
(`is_pro_compliant()` is a hardcoded TODO, and `config_factory.rs:166`
still TODOs `OKTradeCoreBridge.isProAppMode()`). Across every spot order
interactor the value is *pushed in* by Native via `update_is_pro(bool)` —

name: set_margin_switch_open_trading
doc:
Bug V-d (Round 22 · 2026-05-21) — Bridge pushes live
`MarginSwitchView.marginSwitchMode` toggle into the Rust state for
the simple-account / TRADING-level switch.

V1 reference: `MarginSwitchView.kt:231-234` holds the live toggle in
`_marginSwitchMode` MutableStateFlow. The Rust `MarginSwitchManager`
for TRADING level (`account_level == "1"`) always returns `false`
from storage (`margin_switch_manager.rs:263-280`) because the
TRADING-level switch is not persisted — it is held in-memory only.
Without this setter, Round 20 NF-10 (commit `39d67ca5bb`) wired
the flow subscriber but only called `fetchMaxAvailable()` —
downstream derives (`can_borrow`, `is_available_help_tips_visible`,
`is_fund_source_chevron_visible`) never flipped because their
upstream Rust state mirror (`is_margin_mode_on` /
`is_margin_switch_open_trading`) was never written.

This setter is the single-writer rail for the live toggle:
1. Writes `is_margin_mode_on` (Path-2 input of `derive_can_borrow`).
2. Writes `is_margin_switch_open_trading` (chevron-derive input).
3. Runs `recompute_borrow_derives` so `can_borrow` +
`is_available_help_tips_visible` + downstream borrow-family
derives flip in one tick.
4. Re-runs `account::derive_is_fund_source_chevron_visible` so the
chevron hides in lockstep with the help-tips becoming visible
(V1 invariant — see audit report §1.3).
